title: HMRC's Connect data-matching system: about £4.6 billion of additional yield in 2024–25
summary: HMRC's Connect data-matching system yielded ~£4.6bn extra tax in 2024–25 per FOI; C&AG confirms its use to stop risky repayments
account: HM Revenue & Customs launched Connect in 2010–11. Its annual report calls it an IT system that joins a billion pieces of data across its tax regimes to help identify fraud. In a freedom-of-information response reported by Pinsent Masons on 8 October 2025, HMRC said Connect cases generated an average £3.4 billion of additional annual yield. It was about £4.6 billion in 2024–25, with around 4,300 staff using it. The Comptroller and Auditor General's report in HMRC's 2024–25 accounts records that HMRC used TRUCE (Transaction Risking Upstream in a Connect Environment). It served to identify and stop VAT and income-tax repayments needing investigation. IDRS replaced it from August 2023. Official sources describe data analytics and risk rules, not AI.
purpose: Match and analyze data from many sources to identify tax non-compliance and risky repayment claims
system: HMRC Connect (data-matching and risk analytics) and TRUCE (Transaction Risking Upstream in a Connect Environment)
domain: Tax administration: compliance and fraud detection
taxonomy_note: Tax yield is read as the authority's revenue; Trustible's description is written for product sales.

ratings.reason: Aggregate yield with no discrete attributable event.
The £4.6 billion figure is HMRC's own annual attribution via FOI, not an audited event.

ai_role.statement: Yield attribution to Connect comes from HMRC's FOI response as reported by Pinsent Masons. No independent evaluation apportions yield between the system and caseworkers. The NAO's audit report describes TRUCE/IDRS as automated risk-assessment of repayment claims whose controls it reviewed, without quantifying stopped repayments. The cited sources describe the system as data analytics and risk rules rather than machine learning.

later.note: HMRC's 2025-26 annual report, ordered printed on 9 July 2026, says that AI and advanced analytics enabled the protection and recovery of £10 billion in tax in 2025-26 and that a Chief AI Officer was appointed in April 2026; the report does not name Connect.
later.quote: Artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced analytics has already enabled the protection and recovery of £10 billion in tax between 2025 and 2026, and we are continuing to work at pace in this area, appointing our first ever Chief AI Officer in April 2026, to provide clear leadership and ensure the AI advancements that we make are responsible.
